mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public / commissioner for oaths in the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if the issuing jurisdiction is not an Apostille member)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Incumbency for every corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry / companies house in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Apostille registries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized beneficial ownership declaration and source of funds statement disclosing the full chain above the 25% UBO threshold

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as required by the originating state

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of all directors, officers, incorporators, UBOs, and material counterparties against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list and the 50% Rule, and FINTRAC-compliant domestic politically exposed person (PEP) and heads of international organization registers. Positive PEP hits require enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, and senior management approval where required by PCMLTFA. Screening must be repeated before bank account opening and before first UberEats/DoorDash payout processing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registries and Online Services – Corporate Online
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be submitted in English or French using the Latin alphabet. Non-Latin-script brand names require a certified transliteration into Latin characters, which becomes the controlling name for NUANS search and confusion analysis. The legal element 'Unlimited Liability Company' or the abbreviation 'ULC' is mandatory. The name must be distinctive, not confusing with existing names or marks, and not primarily descriptive of the ghost kitchen business.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may: (1) file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of Companies through BC Registries and Online Services within 30 days of rejection, specifying the grounds why the proposed name is distinctive and not confusing; (2) if reconsideration is refused, apply to the Supreme Court of British Columbia for judicial review of the registrar's decision; or (3) submit a revised name for a new name examination. An extension of a valid name reservation may be requested online before expiry; after expiry a new name reservation and new fee are required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address in British Columbia is permissible as a registered office only if it is a real street address, not a post office box, at which legal process can be served under the BC Business Corporations Act. This does not satisfy the ghost kitchen operational substance requirement: the delivery-only food preparation facility must have a separate, non-virtual municipal business-licensed and health-approved commercial kitchen address. Tax substance planning should maintain actual management and decision-making records in BC if the ULC is relied on as a treaty-eligible entity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (approximately 85-95%) at least one unannounced inspection in the first 12 months. The operating kitchen will be subject to unannounced inspections by the regional health authority under the Public Health Act and by municipal by-law enforcement for food safety, zoning, and business licensing compliance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57 (British Columbia), as amended, including the provisions governing incorporation (ss. 12–21), registered office (s. 22), directors (Part 2, Div 4), and unlimited liability company status; and the BC Business Corporations Regulation, BC Reg 265/2001.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance (Victoria, British Columbia)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 – Incorporation Application and Form 2 – Notice of Articles
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital or escrow requirement under BC law; shares may be issued for no consideration or nominal value as determined by the board, subject to full payment when called.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscriber in the Incorporation Application hereby subscribes for 1,000 Class A voting common shares and 1,000 Class B non-voting common shares of the Company, subject to call by directors. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be established at [Address], Vancouver, British Columbia, and [Corporate Services Provider] be appointed Corporate Agent for service of process. RESOLVED, that [A], [B] and [C] be appointed as directors of the Company, and [A] as Chief Executive Officer, [B] as Chief Financial Officer, and [C] as Corporate Secretary, each to serve until the next annual general meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services – Corporate Registry (Corporate Online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access Corporate Online and perform a BC company name search for the proposed 'ghost kitchen' brand names. If a preferred name is available, submit a Name Reservation Request to reserve the name for 56 days. Alternatively, select a numbered company (e.g., 1234567 B.C. Ltd.) to avoid delay.
required_dossiers: Name search report from BC Registry
Certificate of Authorization for corporate agent (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to conflict with an existing trademark or corporate name, file a Request for Reconsideration with the Registrar within 30 days of refusal; if reconsideration fails, select an alternate name and submit a new reservation application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Filing of Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services – Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Incorporation Application (Form 1) and integrated Notice of Articles (Form 2), stating the company has unlimited liability of its shareholders. Provide registered office address in British Columbia, director names and consents, share structure, and any restriction on share transfers. File via Corporate Online (recommended), mail, or in person at the Victoria Corporate Registry. E-filing generally issues a Certificate of Incorporation in minutes.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles (if other than model Articles)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a notice to correct (defective application), the filer has 30 days to resubmit corrected forms; a request for extension may be made; if correction not made, the application is deemed withdrawn.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Organizational Recordkeeping
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries – Corporate Registry (and Board of Directors)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon payment and filing, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation. Convene an inaugural board meeting via unanimous written resolution, adopt the pro-forma first board resolution, issue share certificates to subscribers, appoint officers, and set up the corporate minute book, seal, and registers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains an error, apply under section 33 of the BCA for a Certificate of Correction with supporting evidence, no additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and BC Ministry of Finance – Provincial Tax Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the CRA Business Registration Online form to obtain the Business Number (BN), GST/HST registration (required if gross revenues exceed $30,000 CAD), and payroll deduction account. On the BC Provincial Tax portal, register for PST (sales tax), and confirm employer health tax obligations. Provide the incorporation number and registered office address.
required_dossiers: Corporate registered office and directors list
Estimated annual revenue and employment payroll
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the registration, resubmit corrected information via the 'Business Registration Online' or contact CRA Business Enquiries; PST account can be backdated to the incorporation date with HST/PST returns.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: WorkSafeBC and Employer Health Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: WorkSafeBC (Registration Department) and BC Ministry of Finance (Employer Health Tax)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with WorkSafeBC using the BC BIN (Business Number) and first pay period information. Obtain workers' compensation insurance clearance. Determine employer health tax liability; the employer health tax applies to annual BC remuneration greater than $500,000, otherwise an exemption election can be filed. Keep payroll records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If WorkSafeBC assesses an account late penalty, submit a business registration date correction and request retroactive coverage; EHT registrations can be amended online without penalty if under the threshold.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Food Premises Operating Permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Business Licensing Division (e.g., City of Vancouver) and Regional Health Authority (e.g., Vancouver Coastal Health/Fraser Health) – Environmental Health Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the municipal business licence application for food service with the city; then submit an application for a food premises operating permit with the regional health authority, including scaled floor plans, template of menu, washroom and grease trap details. Book a pre-opening health inspection. Receive the permit before commencing delivery-only food preparation operations.
required_dossiers: HACCP plan or food safety plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the health authority requires modifications, respond to the 'non-compliance report' by making necessary changes and requesting re-inspection; if the municipal licence is denied, appeal to the municipal licensing board or the Supreme Court of British Columbia.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Fire Rescue (e.g., Vancouver Fire and Rescue Services) and BC Ministry of Environment – Environmental Protection Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange for structural load assessment from a registered professional engineer to meet BC Building Code for commercial kitchen equipment. Obtain a fire inspection certificate for commercial cooking exposer and hood/suppression systems. If the ghost kitchen will discharge cooking wastewater or generate commercial grease, register under the municipal sewer bylaw and BC Environmental Management Act; obtain a Permit to Operate or waste registration as required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If fire inspection identifies overdue suppression system service, complete corrective maintenance and reschedule inspection; for ENV non-compliance, submit a compliance plan and schedule to the regional director; unresolved items may be escalated to a ministerial order.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Provincial Health Authority (Vancouver Coastal Health / Fraser Health) – Environmental Health; City Business Licensing Department; BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Premises Operating Permit (Public Eating Establishment / Ghost Kitchen) and Municipal Business Licence (Food Service Establishment)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy (Environmental Protection Division)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration – Small-Scale Food Preparation Facility (no full EIA required unless annual throughput or waste discharge exceeds trigger thresholds)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Environmental Management Act (SBC 2003, c 53) and Municipal Wastewater Regulation (BC Reg 87/2012) – BOD ≤ 300 mg/L, TSS ≤ 300 mg/L, FOG ≤ 50 mg/L; kitchen exhaust vented through certified grease filters and local odour/fugitive emission control; solid waste and organic waste hauled under Regional District bylaw with compostable diversion requirement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire suppression system inspection certificate (NFPA 96), structural load inspection certified by an engineer under BC Building Code, WorksafeBC occupational health and safety clearance, and municipal occupancy permit as a food-related industrial use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including Business Registration Online and My Business Account; British Columbia Ministry of Finance, including eTaxBC, administers British Columbia provincial sales tax and related provincial tax accounts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Canadian ULC incorporated in British Columbia generally obtains a nine-digit CRA Business Number through CRA Business Registration Online or Form RC1, Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts. The corporation then registers the applicable CRA program accounts, including RC for corporate income tax, RT for GST/HST, RP for payroll deductions, and RM for import-export activities. A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada or making taxable supplies in Canada may apply for a Business Number and the relevant GST/HST, corporate income tax, payroll, and import-export accounts through Business Registration Online, Form RC1, or the CRA Non-Resident Registration Web Form. The applicant must provide legal name, jurisdiction and date of incorporation, registered office, Canadian business address, directors, authorized representative, activities, expected revenue, fiscal period, and banking or customs information where requested. The GST/HST account is effective from the required registration date or an earlier voluntary registration date accepted by the CRA. A business making taxable supplies in British Columbia may separately register for a provincial PST number with the British Columbia Ministry of Finance through eTaxBC or the applicable provincial registration process. A CRA Business Number is not itself a GST/HST registration; the RT program account identifies the GST/HST account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada generally treats a British Columbia ULC as a corporation subject to corporate income tax; Canada has no United States-style check-the-box election permitting a Canadian ULC to elect disregarded-entity or partnership status for Canadian tax purposes. For United States federal tax purposes, an eligible Canadian ULC may generally elect its classification under United States Treasury Regulations section 301.7701-3 by filing IRS Form 8832, subject to United States ownership and eligibility rules. The United States default classification depends on the number and status of owners. A United States election does not change the ULC's Canadian legal form or Canadian entity-level tax status. Canadian hybrid-mismatch rules, treaty limitations, foreign tax credit rules, and anti-avoidance provisions must be reviewed where the United States classification differs from the Canadian classification. Canadian corporations may make other specific statutory elections, such as elections under section 85 of the Income Tax Act for qualifying transfers, but these are not entity-classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST), with Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) applying in participating provinces, and separate British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST). British Columbia is not an HST province. A British Columbia ghost-kitchen operator generally considers GST on taxable supplies and PST on taxable goods, software, taxable services, and other specified items under British Columbia law.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST registration is generally required when a person is no longer a small supplier, ordinarily when worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or exceed CAD 30,000 over four consecutive calendar quarters. Associated persons and specified supplies may affect the calculation. Voluntary registration is generally available before the threshold is exceeded, subject to CRA conditions. There is no single equivalent CAD 30,000 threshold for all British Columbia PST obligations; PST registration depends on the nature and location of taxable sales, leasing, use, or provision of taxable goods and services. A restaurant or prepared-food operator must analyze the specific provincial PST treatment of prepared food, delivery charges, equipment, software, and other inputs.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no general nationwide real-time electronic invoicing or pre-clearance mandate for ordinary private-sector GST/HST transactions. A registrant must issue GST/HST documentation containing the information required by the Excise Tax Act and its regulations, retain reliable books and records, and provide prescribed invoices or receipts when requested by customers or the CRA. Electronic invoices and records are generally acceptable if they preserve integrity, accessibility, readability, and auditability. CRA digital services include Business Registration Online and My Business Account; they do not constitute universal real-time invoice clearance. British Columbia does not generally require universal invoice-by-invoice fiscal clearance for private businesses. Separate electronic customs filing requirements may apply through the Canada Border Services Agency, including the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS), and platform, payment processor, consumer-protection, and record-retention requirements may apply independently.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada may generally be zero-rated for GST where the statutory export conditions are satisfied and the supplier retains evidence that the goods were exported, including evidence of delivery or shipment outside Canada and compliance with applicable documentary requirements. Services supplied to a non-resident may be zero-rated only where the specific exported-service provisions apply. The analysis depends on the recipient's residency, the place and manner of performance, the nature of the service, and exclusions for services relating to Canadian real property, tangible personal property situated in Canada, personal services physically performed in Canada, and other excluded categories. Digital, marketing, platform, and administrative services require separate classification. Food preparation and delivery performed for Canadian customers in British Columbia are ordinarily domestic taxable supplies and are not converted into zero-rated exports merely because a customer uses a foreign-owned delivery platform or an offshore payment account. GST registrants may claim input tax credits for eligible GST incurred in commercial activities, subject to documentary and timing requirements. A non-resident person may qualify for limited rebates only under specific statutory programs; there is no general export refund solely because the supplier is non-resident.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) export declaration or other applicable Canada Border Services Agency export reporting record, unless an exemption applies
Commercial invoice identifying exporter, consignee, description, quantity, value, currency, and delivery terms
Bill of lading, airway bill, courier manifest, or equivalent transport documentation
Proof of export or delivery outside Canada, such as carrier records, customs exit evidence, delivery confirmation, or foreign import documentation
Purchase order, contract, customer invoice, and correspondence establishing the non-resident recipient and the nature of the exported supply
Certificate of origin or other preferential-origin documentation where a trade agreement or customer requirement applies
Evidence supporting the GST/HST treatment, including recipient residency records and the statutory zero-rating provision relied upon

Inward remittance or banking evidence where relevant to commercial substantiation, audit support, or a foreign exchange control requirement; Canada does not generally require an Inward Remittance Certificate as a condition for ordinary GST zero-rating
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds be repatriated within 180 days, and there is no general foreign-exchange-control rule imposing a mandatory 180-day remittance deadline on Canadian exporters. Export zero-rating is subject to CRA audit, reassessment, documentary verification, and recovery of improperly uncollected GST or improperly claimed input tax credits or rebates. The CRA may assess the tax, deny input tax credits or rebates, charge arrears interest, and impose penalties for failure to collect, remit, file, maintain records, or provide adequate evidence. A false statement or omission attributable to fraud or gross negligence may attract a penalty generally equal to the greater of CAD 100 and 50% of the understated tax or overstated credit or rebate, subject to the applicable statutory calculation. Repeated or intentional non-compliance may result in gross-negligence or criminal penalties, prosecution, fines, and imprisonment under the Excise Tax Act. False customs declarations may result in Canada Border Services Agency Administrative Monetary Penalties, seizure, forfeiture, reassessment of duties or taxes, and prosecution. British Columbia PST assessed as unpaid or improperly exempted may also be reassessed with interest and provincial penalties. Records supporting zero-rating should generally be retained for the statutory record-retention period, commonly six years from the end of the relevant period, unless a longer period is required by law, objection, appeal, audit, investigation, or litigation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada applies a free-floating CAD with full current- and capital-account convertibility; no exchange-control approval is required for inbound equity, inbound loans, trade settlement, or profit repatriation. Profit remittance from a British Columbia ULC is restricted only by Canadian withholding-tax compliance: Part XIII tax (default 25% on dividends) and possible treaty recharacterization benefits or penalties under the applicable Canada income-tax convention, not by FX rationing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, mandatory conversion, or deadline applies to export proceeds in Canada. Exporters may retain receipts in CAD or foreign currency; FINTRAC cross-border reporting applies to movements of funds over CAD 10,000; corporate-tax and GST/HST reporting still require the underlying receipts to be recognized and documented.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-moderate for a standalone offshore EMI; it cannot substitute for a Schedule I bank account because taking deposits or clearing CAD requires Canadian banking authorization. An offshore digital EMI may be acceptable only as a secondary payout or collection rail if it is registered with FINTRAC as an MSB and operates through a Canadian partner bank; the primary treasury relationship should remain at a tier-1 domestic bank to support DoorDash and UberEats payouts and FINTRAC-compliant reconciliation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily absolute under PCMLTFA, but tier-1 bank policy for a non-resident-owned BC ULC generally requires at least one director or authorized signatory to complete an in-branch or notarized KYC interview. Remote or video onboarding is possible only for low-risk, already-banked clients; appointing a Canadian-resident authorized signatory or legal counsel as authorized agent materially accelerates account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Non-resident ownership combined with an uncommon unlimited-liability corporate structure (ULC), triggering enhanced due diligence and possible classification as a tax-driven or opaque vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: BC incorporation certificate, registry good-standing search, complete ULC articles or articles of continuation, register of shareholders and individuals with significant control, notarized passport copies, source-of-funds bank statements for each non-resident shareholder, and a board resolution authorizing the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Delivery-only ghost kitchen with no physical storefront, multi-brand layering, and high daily payout density that may resemble a shell operation or money-mule network.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed ghost-kitchen facility lease, municipal and BC food-primary licenses, Fraser Health permits, UberEats and DoorDash merchant agreements with merchant IDs, historical payout reports, brand-ownership or trademark records for virtual brands, inventory and supplier invoices, and monthly profit-and-loss evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: High-volume, fragmented third-party delivery payouts accumulating in one account and creating unexplained spikes inconsistent with normal restaurant cash-cycle profiles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Delivery-platform settlement files, daily order-level reconciliation exports, POS and order-management system reports, GST/HST and employer-payroll filings, and a documented treasury policy requiring every clearing deposit to match a platform transaction reference.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the investor's bank to the ULC's tier-1 Canadian bank account, quoting the beneficiary bank, transit and account number, and remittance field 'capital contribution / paid-up capital for BC ULC'. Canada does not prescribe a national FX purpose code, but the receiving bank will request a director resolution, share-subscription documents, and recent investor bank statements; all cross-border transactions of CAD 10,000 or above are FINTRAC reportable. Receive CAD and convert to USD only when an actual operational FX requirement exists, and keep the invoice and subscription paper trail aligned.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier and operating disbursements are cleared via SWIFT MT103 for international vendor payments, via LVTS and ACSS commercial EFT for Canadian-dollar domestic payments, and via documentary or standby letters of credit for bulk food or POS imports requiring transport-document collateral. Cash disbursements are prohibited; every payment must carry the supplier invoice and platform settlement reference. For recurring local services, Interac e-Transfer or direct deposit may be used below FINTRAC thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forwards under ISDA/CSA or bank master agreement
vanilla FX options with a Canadian Schedule I bank
non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for illiquid or restricted currencies not clearing in CAD/USD

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report of the unlimited liability company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Province of British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fee applies after the 60-day filing window; failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Registrar to administratively strike off or dissolve the ULC under the BC Business Corporations Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, including British Columbia provincial corporate income tax allocation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before six months after the ULC's taxation year-end; a T2 return is required every taxation year even if no tax is payable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months; repeated failure may incur higher penalties, and prescribed interest compounds daily.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Provincial Sales Tax annual return and remittance, if approved as an annual PST filer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Ministry of Finance, Taxation and Revenue Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers submit by the last day of the third month after the calendar year-end; monthly or quarterly filers follow the ministry-assigned schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 10% of the assessed PST plus interest for late filing or late remittance; the ministry may require security for repeated non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory-register and minute-book verification certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maintained by the ULC's corporate agent or registered office; available for production to directors, shareholders, auditors, and regulators on demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed before the BC Annual Report is filed and updated at each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or incomplete registers expose directors and officers to offences under the BCBCA and may invalidate corporate filings; no separate administrative strike-off consequence applies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No monetary revenue, asset, or size threshold under BCBCA triggers a compulsory audit for a private ULC. A mandatory independent audit applies only if the ULC is a public company, if shareholders validly require an auditor, or if a unanimous shareholder agreement, lender, franchisor, or regulatory condition imposes an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private ULCs in British Columbia may report under CPA Canada Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or IFRS. If the ULC becomes publicly accountable, IFRS is mandatory. The books and records must permit the preparation of financial statements compliant with the applicable framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the BCBCA, the ULC must maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC Register). At each annual report date, directors must review the register, record any change in significant control, including share transfers affecting 25% or more of voting rights or value, and certify the register's accuracy. There is no separate public annual UBO filing; the register must be produced for lawful official inspection.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control
Minute Book containing shareholder and director resolutions and meeting minutes

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined general corporate income tax rate (15% federal Part I under ITA s.123 plus 12% British Columbia provincial general rate under BC Income Tax Act s.5), applicable to a BC unlimited liability corporation not qualifying as a Canadian-controlled private corporation.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays for ghost kitchen operators. Available preferences: (i) CCPC small business deduction (9% federal + 2% BC = 11% on first CAD 500,000 active business income) is unavailable to a ULC controlled directly or indirectly by non-residents; (ii) Clean Technology Investment Tax Credit of 30% refundable for qualifying zero-emission kitchen and refrigeration equipment acquired before 2035; (iii) Accelerated Investment Incentive permitting up to 1.5x or 3x first-year capital cost allowance for eligible property acquired before 2028; (iv) SR&ED credits are generally not applicable to delivery-only food preparation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return for federal and BC provincial corporate income tax; filed electronically through CRA-certified E-file software or the CRA 'My Business Account' portal using the corporation's business number (BC) program account; the T2 covers both federal Part I tax and BC provincial tax on the single return (BC Schedule 5 for provincial calculation).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual T2 return for each taxation year; quarterly corporate tax instalments for federal and BC tax where estimated combined liability exceeds CAD 3,000; monthly or quarterly GST/HST and payroll source deduction remittances for the operating ghost kitchen.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 must be filed no later than 6 months after the taxation year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end due June 30); final tax balance due no later than 2 months after year-end (3 months only for eligible CCPCs within the small business limit, which a non-resident-owned ULC is not); quarterly instalments due on the last day of each instalment quarter (months 3, 6, 9 and 12 of the taxation year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name, Canada Revenue Agency business number (BN) and program account, jurisdiction of incorporation (British Columbia, BCBCA), incorporation date, taxation year start and end dates, registered office and mailing address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the BC physical kitchen address as the principal establishment; list the non-resident parent and all related foreign entities in the related corporations schedule; attach a treaty residence certificate of the parent only if a treaty-based exemption or reduced rate is relied upon; the ULC must never appear as a mere nominee of the foreign shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate gross business revenue from all virtual brands and delivery-only sales transacted through the BC ghost kitchen, including UberEats and DoorDash proceeds, net of refunds, discounts and delivery platform customer fees where the corporation is the merchant of record.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All revenue generated by Canadian customers must be booked in the T2; directing sales proceeds directly to the foreign parent or avoiding the T2 altogether constitutes an undisclosed permanent establishment and triggers the full audit and penalty regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue less deductible expenses: food and packaging costs, kitchen labour, facility rent, utilities, delivery platform commissions, marketing, insurance, capital cost allowance and head-office charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees, technology royalties and intercompany charges paid to the foreign parent must be arm's length and backed by contemporaneous comparables; excessive payments may be recharacterized under ITA s.247(2) and deemed dividends subject to 25% Part XIII withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after deducting non-capital loss carryforwards (20-year forward, 3-year back), charitable donations and after applying the BC permanent establishment allocation formula in T2 Schedule 5.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners should ensure loss schedules are supported by audited financial statements; BC source income is allocated to the province using the standard revenue, payroll and fixed-asset formula; do not claim losses of the foreign parent against BC income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal corporate tax computed at the 15% general rate on taxable income, reduced by federal tax credits and investment tax credits, including the refundable Clean Technology ITC if claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the ULC is not claiming the CCPC small business deduction unless it is in fact Canadian-controlled; a false CCPC election by a US-owned ULC is treated as misrepresentation and reassessed with gross negligence penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: BC provincial corporate tax at 12% of taxable income allocated to BC, computed on the T2 provincial schedule (BC Schedule 5) and carried to the provincial section of the T2 summary page.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Income from delivery sales made through the BC kitchen is 100% allocated to BC; interprovincial allocation is not available for a single-location ULC; under-allocation to BC will trigger BC revenue audit and penalty assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total federal and BC tax payable less instalments, federal and provincial credits, refundable credits and the amount of any overpayment; the resulting balance is due on the statutory due date and bears interest from the due date until paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If dividends are declared to the foreign parent, the withholding tax is a separate Part XIII remittance made through the NR4 process and cannot be netted against the line 420 balance due.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim of capital allowances on kitchen equipment (Class 8, 20% declining balance), point-of-sale and computer systems (Class 50, 55% declining balance), leasehold improvements (Class 13) and building improvements (Class 1, 4% or 6%).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim CCA on assets still owned by the foreign parent or on assets leased from the parent at inflated values; CRA may disallow the deduction and reallocate income under s.247.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the unpaid tax balance plus 1% per full month up to 12 months, imposed on both federal and BC portions; compound daily interest accrues at the CRA prescribed rate on all unpaid amounts. Late or deficient instalments attract a penalty equal to 50% of the arrears interest on the shortfall. Failure to file T106 information returns: CAD 100 per day, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500 per return. Gross negligence penalty: 50% of the understated tax for knowingly or grossly negligent misrepresentations. Second-offence late filing penalties and interest are higher under ITA s.162(2).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Treaty-reduced withholding is applied at source where the BC ULC obtains and retains on file a completed Form NR301 (individual recipient) or NR302 (corporate recipient) together with a foreign residence certificate (TRC) issued by the recipient's residence state, such as IRS Form 6166 for a US parent. No CRA pre-approval is required; the payer must remit the Part XIII amount by the 15th day of the month following each payment and remain liable for any shortfall if the recipient is not the beneficial owner. Under the Canada-US Treaty, the dividend rate is 5% where a US corporation owns at least 10% of the ULC's voting shares and otherwise 15%; for non-treaty jurisdictions, the full 25% statutory rate applies unless the DTA provides otherwise.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII withholding: 25% on royalties and 25% on interest. Canada-US Treaty: royalties for use of IP 10% (Art. XII); interest 0% for arm's-length interest (Art. XI) and 15% for contingent interest; non-treaty arm's-length interest may be exempt under s.212(1)(b)(vii). Management fees or service fees paid to the foreign parent that exceed arm's-length value may be recharacterized as dividends or royalties and attract the applicable Part XIII rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 aggregate fair market value per reportable transaction category with non-arm's-length non-residents in the taxation year triggers the mandatory T106 information return and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; Country-by-Country Report filing is required only for MNE groups with consolidated group revenue exceeding CAD 900,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada and British Columbia have no statutory Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to UAE ESR, but substance is enforced through: (i) the general anti-avoidance rule (ITA s.245) which denies benefits of avoidance transactions lacking economic substance; (ii) the common law sham doctrine and 'central management and control' residence rules; (iii) treaty limitation-on-benefits provisions (Canada-US Treaty Art. XXIX-A) requiring genuine business purpose; and (iv) provincial licensing and payroll records creating a rebuttable presumption of a permanent establishment in BC. A ULC that contracts for delivery sales but has no employees, no leased kitchen premises, no equipment and no operational management in BC is fatally deficient.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of cash-based delivery revenue, fabricated expense invoices, false CCA claims, understatement of BC-source income, or instructing delivery platforms to route sales proceeds to the foreign parent without recording them in the ULC accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under ITA s.239(1), tax evasion is punishable by a fine of 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment for up to 2 years on summary conviction; CRA may also reassess beyond the normal 4-year limitation period and impose a 50% gross negligence penalty under s.163(2); GST/HST evasion carries additional penalties under the Excise Tax Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who direct, acquiesce in or benefit from the evasion are prosecuted as parties under Criminal Code s.21; civil restitution orders, freezing injunctions, departure bans as bail conditions, and personal liability under ITA s.227.1 for unremitted payroll source deductions and GST/HST apply; fraudulent conveyance actions against shareholders under BC law are available to CRA.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Sham and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the ULC as a conduit with no employees, no bank account in Canada, no physical kitchen, no board meetings in Canada, and no commercial substance while claiming Canada-US treaty benefits and allocating income to a zero-rate jurisdiction; deliberately using the ULC's unlimited liability feature as a mere flow-through vehicle for US tax without operational reality.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA will disregard the entity under the sham doctrine, reassess the foreign parent as having a permanent establishment in Canada, disallow treaty benefits under the LOB clause, apply GAAR under s.245 to recharacterize the arrangement, and assess the full Canadian tax plus interest, penalties of up to 50% of the avoided tax, and potential Part XIII withholding on deemed dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the BC Business Corporations Act, shareholders of an unlimited liability company are jointly and severally liable on the corporation's dissolution for corporate debts; directors face personal liability for unpaid wages under the BC Employment Standards Act and for unremitted source deductions under ITA s.227.1; courts may issue travel bans pending criminal prosecution and civil asset forfeiture orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, Money Laundering and FINTRAC Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Handling large cash deliveries without a FINTRAC compliance program, deliberately structuring transactions to avoid the CAD 10,000 reporting threshold, transacting with sanctioned or fraudulent virtual brand partners, processing refunds through shell payment accounts, or failing to register and report as a money services business where payment handling crosses into MSB activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, administrative monetary penalties of up to CAD 1,000,000 per violation may be imposed on corporations; criminal money laundering under Criminal Code s.462.31 carries imprisonment up to 10 years on indictment and unlimited fines; BC's Civil Forfeiture Act permits in rem forfeiture of the kitchen assets and bank balances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who authorized, directed or acquiesced in the laundering are personally criminally liable; restraint and freezing orders under Criminal Code s.462.33, Canadian departure bans, large personal fines and restitution orders are routinely sought; directorial disqualification and personal civil liability follow a conviction.
